subject: Pilot synthesis: model recommendations and quantization path
messages:
From: Charlie Huang <charlie@lumenhealth.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ml-team@lumenhealth.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumen pilot discovery — follow-up and sample artifacts

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from our side and a couple of asks before we lock the pilot scope.

What we heard on the call (high level):
- Primary use case: clinical note condensation + extraction (summaries for care teams).
- SLO targets: p50 latency <= 120ms; steady throughput target ~80 req/s; peak bursts to 250 req/s.
- Context: average convo length ~1,200 tokens, worst-case 4,096.
- Success metrics: F1 on extraction tasks >= 0.78 vs internal gold, summary ROUGE-L delta <= 0.03 compared to current baseline.

What we can share now: attached is a sanitized prompt set and a small eval sample (lumen-promptset-v1.json). We ran a light local eval across a couple of open models — we saw decent throughput with 7B-family but quality gap on longer contexts.

Primary asks for Redwood:
1) Recommended model candidates for a pilot (we prefer smaller latency/cost but won’t sacrifice core metric thresholds).
2) A suggested quantization/run-time path (AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8) and estimated delta in F1/ROUGE we should expect.
3) A short mutual action plan and who at Redwood will run the benchmark.

Also looping procurement (procurement@lumenhealth.ai) for early visibility — they may have questions about reserved capacity pricing if this becomes prod.

Thanks — happy to run any additional samples if helpful.

—Charlie
Director, NLP Engineering
Lumen Health
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Charlie Huang <charlie@lumenhealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lumen pilot discovery — follow-up and sample artifacts

Charlie — thanks for the clear summary and the prompt set. Good notes from the call. Below is a concise proposal and next steps so we can get a lightweight pilot started early next week.

Quick recommendation (pilot scope):
- Candidate models to evaluate (order of preference for this use case):
  1) llama-2-13b-chat (FP16 baseline) — strong long-context generalization, good out-of-the-box summarization.
  2) orca-mini-13b (AWQ-friendly) — often close to 13B quality with reduced memory when using AWQ.
  3) falcon-7b-instruct (GPTQ) — good latency/cost tradeoff for shorter contexts; may degrade on long clinical notes.

Quantization/run-time path we suggest for the pilot:
- Baseline: run FP16 on a sample set for ground-truth quality numbers (we’ll report F1/ROUGE baseline).
- Path A (low-risk): AWQ on orca-mini-13b then validate on full prompt set. Expect F1 delta ~ -0.01 to -0.04 depending on prompt sensitivity; ROUGE impact usually small but check edge cases for numeric extraction.
- Path B (cost-first): GPTQ on falcon-7b-instruct/llama-13b — can yield better throughput but higher variance in entity extraction; expect F1 delta ~ -0.02 to -0.06 in our experience.
- Path C (experimental / hardware dependent): FP8 (if supported end-to-end) — promising throughput gains but requires careful compiler/runtime support and per-model validation; quality delta uncertain.

Operational tuning notes (what we’ll test):
- KV-cache warmup policy and prefix caching for longer notes.
- Dynamic batching to hit 80 req/s p50 while bounding tail latency.
- Request routing: keep critical extraction calls on FP16 hot-path, route lower-priority summarization to quantized variants for cost savings.

Next steps / ownership:
- Redwood will: run a 3-model micro-benchmark (FP16 llama-13b, AWQ orca-mini-13b, GPTQ falcon-7b) across your prompt set and return a concise tradeoff spreadsheet (Marissa).
- Karthik will prepare a quantization playbook with expected deltas and tunables (batching, sequence length knobs).
- Ben will validate throughput/latency on a Dedicated pod simulating 80 req/s baseline and 250 req/s peak.

Deliverables and timing:
- Benchmark results + short deck: 3 business days after we receive the full sample set (we have a small sample already; if you can share the ~200-row eval set we’ll run the full pass).
- Mutual action plan doc (draft attached): redwood-mutual-action-plan-20270118.docx

Attachments we included for the pilot: benchmark-results-20270113.csv (sample run), redwood-mutual-action-plan-20270118.docx.

Would you be available for a 30-min touchpoint on Monday 18 Jan to review preliminary results? If so, we’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Karthik: draft the quantization playbook notes (AWQ/GPTQ tuning knobs, expected F1/ROUGE variance, fallback rules). Keep it <2 pages; we’ll include as an appendix to the mutual action plan.
- Ben: spin a Dedicated test pod with simulated 80 req/s steady-state and 250 req/s peak; capture p50/p95/p99 latencies for each model/quant combo.

Procurement: Hannah — I’ll draft a high-level reserved-capacity note (monthly commit tiers) and mark it for procurement@lumenhealth.ai. We should propose an initial 3-month pilot commit for predictable baseline throughput.

I’ll consolidate and send the calendar invite for 11:00 PT. If Charlie uploads the eval set to the secure S3 link, share the link to me and Marissa.

Thanks — short and focused here; we’ll iterate after the run.

Hannah
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
